anti_patterns: Accepting optimistic or unfinalized headers as proof of finality: a source-chain reorg turns every downstream mint or release into unbacked liability
Trusting relayer-submitted headers without on-chain consensus verification: this silently downgrades the bridge to a single-relayer multisig
Hardcoding the validator set or sync committee without rotation logic: the client stops following the chain at the first epoch or period boundary
Storing full block headers on chain instead of compressed consensus states: unbounded storage growth that repeats the cost the pattern exists to avoid
Skipping misbehaviour submission and client freezing: provable equivocation keeps flowing packets instead of halting the channel
Verifying inclusion proofs against the latest head instead of a finalized commitment root: reorgable state authorizes irreversible execution
Deploying one shared client for unrelated counterparty chains: a consensus failure on one chain contaminates verification for all of them
avoid_when: The source chain has no light-client-friendly finality (no finalized checkpoints, accountable validator set, or verifiable header chain)
Sub-second cross-chain latency is required: execution is bounded by source-chain finality plus relay delay
The bridge connects chains with incompatible or unverifiable state-proof formats and no proof-adapter exists
No party can be relied upon to relay headers at all: with zero live relayers the bridge stalls
Governance cannot manage trusted-checkpoint initialization or consensus-fork upgrades
best_practices: Initialize each client from a socially verified checkpoint (genesis validators root or trusted header) and document the trust ceremony
Require supermajority participation (at least two thirds of the sync committee or validator set) before accepting any header update
Verify inclusion and membership proofs only against finalized commitment roots, never against the speculative head
Implement validator-set and sync-committee rotation as first-class updates tested against epoch and period boundaries
Expose misbehaviour submission so any watcher can freeze the client on provable equivocation, with a governance path to unfreeze
Keep a tested upgrade path for counterparty consensus hard forks (chain-ID revision, fork-version, proof-format changes)
Separate the application-agnostic updater contract from application logic so token, message, and governance use cases share one audited verifier
Bound per-message proof size and verification gas, and load-test client updates under worst-case committee rotation
benefits: Trust minimization: forging a message requires forging source-chain consensus (a validator supermajority), not bribing a small bridge committee
Permissionless relaying: relayers are trusted only for liveness, so anyone can submit headers and proofs and censorship requires stopping every relayer
No custodial committee: there is no fixed multisig whose key compromise mints unbacked assets on the destination chain
Finality-gated execution: mint, release, and delivery act only on finalized commitment roots, inheriting source-chain reorg safety
Provable safety response: detectable consensus violations (equivocation) freeze the client and halt packet flow instead of failing open
Modular reuse: one audited updater and light client serve token transfers, message passing, and arbitrary state reads via Merkle proofs
Minimal on-chain state: compressed consensus states (commitment root plus next-validator information) replace full header chains
component_types: Light Client Contract: on-chain verifier tracking counterparty consensus state and finalized roots
Relayer: off-chain, untrusted process submitting headers, consensus proofs, and misbehaviour evidence
Updater Contract: application-agnostic registry exposing verified headers and commitment roots to applications
Proof Verifier: on-chain BLS aggregate-signature and Merkle or SSZ inclusion-proof checks, optionally compressed behind a zk-SNARK verifier
Application Contract: destination-side logic (mint, release, deliver) acting only on proofs verified against finalized roots
Checkpoint Bootstrapper: initialization flow establishing the first trusted consensus state by social consensus
context: Two sovereign blockchains need to move assets or messages between them without trusting a custodial committee or multisig. The destination chain runs an on-chain light client of the source chain: permissionless relayers submit finalized source headers with consensus proofs (validator-set signatures, sync-committee aggregates), the contract verifies them against its tracked validator set, rotates the set at epoch boundaries, and then verifies Merkle inclusion proofs of the lock, burn, or send event against the finalized commitment root before minting, releasing, or delivering on the destination side
design_principles: Verify consensus, not committees: the verifier checks source-chain consensus rules, never the word of appointed signers
Finalize then execute: only finalized checkpoints authorize state changes on the destination chain
Distrust the transport: relayers need no reputation because every byte they submit is re-verified on chain
Minimize on-chain state: store compressed consensus snapshots sufficient for proof verification, not full history
Fail closed on equivocation: provable misbehaviour freezes verification rather than letting packets keep flowing
Separate verification from application: the bridge proves what happened on the source chain; applications decide what it means
name: light-client-bridge
references: Ethereum annotated-spec, Altair Minimal Light Client sync protocol (sync committees, LightClientSnapshot, LightClientUpdate) - https://github.com/ethereum/annotated-spec/blob/master/altair/sync-protocol.md

technology_stack: IBC and ibc-go (ICS-02 clients, ICS-03 connections, ICS-04 channels and packets)
Ethereum Altair sync committees with BLS12-381 aggregate signatures
SSZ and Merkle inclusion proofs plus ICS-23 commitment proofs
zk-SNARK proof compression of consensus verification (Groth16-style step and rotate circuits)
Production light-client bridges such as Succinct Telepathy and zkBridge-style updater contracts
tradeoffs: High verification cost: naive on-chain consensus verification is extremely expensive (the zkBridge authors report about 64 million gas per Cosmos header on Ethereum), so production bridges add zk-SNARK compression circuits
Latency bounded by source finality: no message can be delivered faster than the source chain finalizes plus relay delay
Quadratic scaling surface: every ordered chain pair needs its own client, connection, and validator-tracking state
Security upper-bounded by the source chain: a supermajority attack on source consensus passes the light client by construction
Complex fork maintenance: consensus hard forks, chain-ID revisions, and proof-format changes require coordinated client upgrades
Liveness depends on at least one honest relayer: safety needs no trusted party but a fully censored relay network stalls the bridge
Trusted initialization: the first checkpoint is accepted axiomatically, so a fraudulent genesis state compromises everything after it
use_cases: Cross-chain token transfers verified against finalized source state (for example Cosmos to Ethereum packet commitments checked against the AppHash)
Cross-chain message passing where the receiver proves the send commitment exists in finalized source state (IBC send, receive, acknowledge, and timeout flows)
Execution-layer state reads on a destination chain proven from finalized beacon headers and execution payloads
Reducing bridge operating cost by compressing consensus verification into succinct proofs verified for a fraction of naive gas cost
